datasets.title: Copernicus Vegetation Index Anomaly (FAPAR Anomaly)
datasets.description: Fraction of Absorbed Photosynthetically Active Radiation (FAPAR) is a biophysical dimensionless quantity (its values range from 0/no absorption to 1/total absorption) used to assess the greenness and health of vegetation. FAPAR anomalies can be used as an indicator to detect and monitor the impacts of agricultural drought on the growth and productivity of vegetation. The data is presented in 10-day time composite of the Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS).. [Source: This metadata record was automatically extracted from the Humanitarian Data Exchange (HDX); Original dataset: https://data.humdata.org/dataset/global-anomalies-fapar-viirs]
datasets.details: Variations in the vegetation health and/or cover could be related to stress factors not related to droughts (e.g., plant diseases, pests, hail, flooding). To determine if changes in FAPAR are linked with a drought event or not, FAPAR data should be interpreted jointly with other indicators (as in the EDO Combined Drought Indicator).

lineage.description: FAPAR values are derived from VIIRS satellite observations in 10-day composites. Anomalies are calculated at each grid cell as the deviation from a long-term mean baseline spanning 2012 to the most recent complete year. This empirical approach enables detection and monitoring of agricultural drought impacts on vegetation growth and productivity across global agricultural regions.

sources.name: Visible Infrared Imaging Radiometer Suite (VIIRS)
sources.description: Satellite-based radiometer providing 10-day composite observations of photosynthetically active radiation absorption used to derive FAPAR measurements

sources.name: European Commission, Joint Research Centre (JRC)
sources.description: Processing and distribution of Copernicus FAPAR anomaly products, including calculation of anomalies relative to long-term baseline
